summary:
MARSWALK is an interactive 3D Martian geospatial information system (GIS), surface survival handbook, and extravehicular activity (EVA) traverse planner built for future human explorers on Mars. While orbital missions have mapped Mars in high detail, raw planetary datasets remain disconnected from human physiological limits. On Mars, a route that looks short on a 2D map can exhaust an astronaut's oxygen supply on a steep sulfate scarp or trap a rover in low-thermal-inertia drift sand.

MARSWALK bridges this gap by reprojecting live NASA Mars Trek WMTS orbital rasters (MGS MOLA, Odyssey THEMIS IR, MGS TES Thermal Inertia, MRO CTX 6 m/px, and MRO HiRISE 25 cm/px) and the USGS Standardized Global Geologic Map (SIM 3292) onto a 3D globe across three distinct landing zones: Jezero Crater, Gale Crater (Mount Sharp), and unexplored Arcadia Planitia. It pairs a 6-chapter NASA-STD-3001 Survival Handbook with a 0.38g sloped metabolic physics engine, automatic hazard-avoidance routing, side-by-side route tradeoff comparisons, a Mars24 solar ephemeris clock, and a 3D Suited EVA Traverse Simulator.
details:
1. WHAT MARSWALK DOES & HOW IT WORKS

MARSWALK transforms authoritative NASA orbital imagery, rover ground-truth telemetry, and human spaceflight standards (NASA-STD-3001) into an operational 6-station Mission Control workstation and survival guide for Mars:

• Station 1 — Mission Overview & Atmospheric Telemetry: Displays live Mars Sol Date (MSD), Coordinated Mars Time (MTC), and longitude-calibrated Local Mean Solar Time (LMST) using the NASA GISS Mars24 algorithm (Allison & McEwen, 2000), alongside surface pressure (610 Pa mean baseline vs. the 6,250 Pa human Armstrong limit), diurnal temperature swings, and Curiosity RAD / NASA DONKI solar particle radiation status.

• Station 2 — Orbital GIS & Survey Lenses: Streams 10+ coregistered NASA Mars Trek WMTS layers and vector catalogs onto an interactive 3D globe. Because NASA Mars Trek serves tiles in Equirectangular projection (EPSG:104905, 2:1 aspect ratio) while 3D WebGL globes require Web Mercator (EPSG:3857), I engineered a custom tile reprojection pipeline that fetches covering Mars Trek tiles and resamples each pixel row via inverse Gudermannian mapping: lat = (180/pi) * arctan(sinh(pi * (1 - 2 * y_merc))). Users can switch between MGS MOLA DEM/Hillshade (463 m/px), MOLA+HRSC Blended DEM (200 m/px), USGS Global Geology (SIM 3292), Odyssey THEMIS Day/Night IR (100 m/px), MGS TES Thermal Inertia & Dust Cover, MRO CTX (6 m/px), MRO HiRISE (25 cm/px), 2,095 CRISM/OMEGA aqueous mineral detections, 1,000 MRO CTX glaciers, and 56 NASA EZMars human exploration zones.

• Station 3 — 0.38g EVA Route Planner & Side-by-Side Hazard Comparison: Allows astronauts to plot custom multi-waypoint traverses across three distinct regions—Jezero Crater (Perseverance MSR Depot & Cheyava Falls), Gale Crater (Curiosity's Proposed Path Up Mount Sharp PIA23179 & 2025 Boxwork Formations PIA26680), and Arcadia Planitia (an unexplored candidate human landing site with shallow SHARAD/SWIM subsurface water ice PIA26046). Every route segment is tested against mapped surface hazards (low-thermal-inertia drift sand <150 TIU, >20° sulfate scarps, and coarse boulder aprons). MARSWALK automatically computes a hazard-bypassing detour (Route A) and compares it side-by-side against a direct shortest-path line (Route B) across distance, slope gradient, Santee et al. (2001) 0.38g metabolic energy expenditure (145 kg suited mass across Solo, 2-Crew Buddy, and Pressurized Rover modes), PLSS oxygen budget (850 L pack with a 20% emergency reserve floor), sublimator cooling water (3.8 L), and cumulative radiation exposure.

• Station 4 — Science & ISRU Target Catalog: Curates 17+ geocoded geological, astrobiological, and In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU) targets with orbital spectral signatures, Perseverance raw rover frames, and sample-return priorities.

• Station 5 — Martian Sky Dome & Solar Ephemeris: Computes topocentric altitude and azimuth for the Sun, Phobos, Deimos, and Earth (via JPL Horizons ephemerides) to schedule daylight EVAs, solar array charging windows, and Earth direct-to-Earth (DTE) communication passes.

• Station 6 — 6-Chapter Martian Survival Handbook: A built-in engineering field manual benchmarking Mars vs. Earth across (1) Atmosphere & Thermal Extremes, (2) 0.38g Spacesuit & PLSS Life Support, (3) Radiation & Solar Particle Storms, (4) Regolith, Dust & Perchlorate Toxicity (0.5–1.0 wt% ClO4-), (5) MOXIE O2 & Subsurface Ice ISRU, and (6) Mars24 Timekeeping & Communications.

• Interactive 3D Suited EVA Traverse Simulator: Lets users rehearse planned traverses on the terrain with a helmet visor HUD, tactical hazard radar, rock-core sampling at NASA waypoints, and an emergency Basecamp Safe House shelter during simulated solar particle events.

2. INTENDED IMPACT & BENEFITS

• For Mission Planners & Educators: Demonstrates how orbital remote sensing (thermal inertia, slope roughness, hydrated mineral spectroscopy, and subsurface radar) directly governs human survival decisions on another planet.

• Scientific Transparency: Explicitly separates direct NASA/USGS orbital and rover observations from physics-based engineering models so every metric can be verified against primary literature.

3. TOOLS, LANGUAGES & SOFTWARE ARCHITECTURE

• Frontend & 3D GIS Engine: TypeScript, Next.js (App Router), React, Tailwind CSS, MapLibre GL JS (3D Globe projection & custom marstrek:// protocol handler), Three.js / React Three Fiber (3D suited astronaut traverse renderer), and Web Audio API.

• Scientific & Physics Modules: Custom TypeScript implementations of Santee et al. (2001) 0.38g sloped locomotion energetics, Allison & McEwen (2000) Mars24 solar timekeeping, and spherical polygon obstacle-avoidance routing.

4. PRE-EVENT RESEARCH, 3D ASSET & API DISCLOSURE

• Prior to the hackathon, I researched planetary GIS projection formats and surface survival benchmarks across NASA/JPL Mars Trek, USGS Astrogeology (SIM 3292), NASA PDS Geosciences Node (MOLA & THEMIS), UAHiRISE, NASA SWIM, NASA GISS Mars24, JPL Horizons, and NASA CCMC DONKI. I also prepared foundational dark-mode UI layout scaffolding and configured API keys for the Groq API and voice synthesis pipeline ahead of time so I could focus the hackathon on building the Martian survival physics engine, Mars Trek reprojection pipeline, obstacle-avoidance router, and 6-chapter Survival Handbook.

• 3D Astronaut Model Attribution: The 3D astronaut character in the surface traverse simulator is adapted from the "Astronaut" model by Antropik on Sketchfab (CC-BY-4.0) and is intentionally rendered not to scale on the globe strictly for traverse simulation visibility.
